A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Near Exact Privacy Amplification for Matrix Mechanisms. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original prefix-sum RMSE experiments, optimization timings, sampling sensitivity analyses, and CIFAR-10 training results, including 100-trial comparisons and additional RMSE plots in Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds results on selected band counts and RMSE sensitivity to sampling probability.

M1.justification: The balls-in-bins construction, Algorithms 1–2, matrix optimization objective and gradients, and padded/truncated batching procedure are retained. V2 makes adjacency-specific verification explicit, but does not establish a changed underlying sampling, noise-generation, or optimization method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate prefix-sum RMSE and CIFAR-10 image classification. Appendix B retains the same nine epoch/iteration combinations. The added sampling-probability sweep varies settings within the existing RMSE task.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the same Poisson, unamplified, banded-matrix, BLT, Toeplitz, and MEMF alternatives. The new sampling-probability comparison uses existing comparators; newly cited concurrent work is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: New Figure 3c fixes 128 training rounds and a target (1, 10^-5)-DP guarantee while varying sampling probability, matching expected batch sizes between methods. This adds a controlled evaluation protocol without replacing the existing CIFAR-10 training protocol.

E4.justification: V2 adds sampling-probability sensitivity analysis in Figure 3c and reports the preferred band count across epsilon values in Figure 3b. Existing timing, Monte Carlo sample-count sensitivity, practical-batching comparisons, and Appendix B analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V1 describes sufficient Monte Carlo sampling and a small verification failure probability without specifying them. V2 reports 10^8 verification samples, tau = 1.25, and failure bounds below 7.2 × 10^-9 per adjacency and 1.5 × 10^-8 jointly. CIFAR's 100 trials and 95% confidence intervals are unchanged; an increase in runs is not established.

E6.justification: Figures 3b–c add band-selection and sampling-probability results; for example, Figure 3c shows greater RMSE reduction for balls-in-bins than Poisson at p = 1/32, 1/64, and 1/128. Existing performance plots, timing values, and all 18 Appendix B plots are unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 adds Theorem 2.2 with a finite-sample concentration bound and proof, revises Lemma 3.2 to distinguish add/remove adjacency, and adds bisection convergence reasoning in Section 4.1. These substantially expand the accountant's formal justification. Appendix A is unchanged. The added proof contains algebraic slips, including an incorrect displayed derivative.

C1.justification: The main claims remain near-exact accounting for general nonnegative lower-triangular matrices, optimization accounting for amplification, improved prefix-sum RMSE, and improved CIFAR-10 utility with practical batching. Abstract wording refinements do not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: The new Figure 7 caption explains why a smaller noise multiplier alone does not imply better learning performance when noise cancellation differs. Section 1.3 also identifies the difficulty of transferring concurrent work's efficient independent-noise samplers to general correlation matrices. Existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: New tables labeled Figures 7–8 disclose per-epsilon CIFAR-10 noise multipliers for four methods and selected band counts for both BandMF sampling schemes. V1 described their selection without listing these values. These are additional reproducibility details, not evidence that the original experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: New Section 1.3 acknowledges Chua et al. (2025) as independently proposing identical batching and contrasts its independent-noise accounting with this work's general matrices. V2 also adds Schuchardt et al. (2024) when discussing replacement adjacency. The broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: V2 adds a concurrent-work subsection, renumbers Future Directions, expands proof explanations, and makes limited wording and bibliographic corrections. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 3 expands from two to four panels, and two CIFAR-10 parameter tables are added as Figures 7–8. Appendix B regrouping places each setting's two existing plots together. Other figures are reused, with relocation, renumbering, and a small Figure 1 caption clarification.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency through explicit privacy-verification bounds, clearer adjacency treatment, CIFAR parameter tables, and additional sensitivity evidence. The gains are limited by retained inconsistencies: Figure 8 lists 32 baseline bands at epsilon = 8 while the prose still says at most 16, and the new proof contains algebraic slips. Overall, the added documentation and context provide a modest net improvement while the principal results remain unchanged.
